item.title: NEW: Critical Citrix Zero-Day Exploited for Weeks Before Discovery
item.description:
Headline: Critical Citrix Zero-Day Exploited for Weeks Before Discovery

Summary:
A critical memory overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-88772) in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway was exploited by suspected state-sponsored actors for over three weeks before public disclosure. Attackers deployed the WHIPSHOT web shell and SLAPSHOT tunneling tool, targeting government and financial institutions across North America and Europe. CISA has added the flaw to its KEV catalog, mandating immediate patching.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Threat Actor

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: A critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-88772) in Citrix NetScaler was actively exploited for weeks, targeting government and financial sectors. Patch now.

item.title: NEW: NetScaler Zero-Days CVE-2026-88771 & CVE-2026-88772 Actively Exploited
item.description:
Headline: NetScaler Zero-Days CVE-2026-88771 & CVE-2026-88772 Actively Exploited

Summary:
Citrix has disclosed two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, in its NetScaler appliances, which are being actively exploited in the wild. The vulnerabilities, both rated with a CVSS score of 9.5, can lead to denial of service or remote code execution. Threat actors have been observed exploiting these flaws since at least August 21, 2026, to deliver web shells, establish initial access, and maintain persistence. Unit 42 analysis identified over 50,000 exposed NetScaler instances and detailed two distinct attack patterns, one involving a crafted DTLS packet and another using a three-stage log poisoning technique to achieve RCE. Immediate patching is critical.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Report

Reading Time: 8 minutes

Meta Description: Unit 42 reports active in-the-wild exploitation of two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, in Citrix NetScaler devices.

item.title: UPDATE: Citrix Patches Two Critical NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Attack
item.description:
Headline: Citrix Patches Two Critical NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Attack

Summary:
Citrix has released emergency patches for eight vulnerabilities in its NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances, with two critical zero-days, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, confirmed to be under active global exploitation. The flaws allow for unauthenticated remote code execution, leading to potential webshell deployment and full network compromise. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added both vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating immediate patching and compromise investigation for federal agencies. The attacks were reportedly underway for weeks prior to disclosure, with attackers gaining persistent access to internal networks. Organizations are urged to apply updates immediately and hunt for indicators of compromise, as patching alone does not remediate existing intrusions.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Patch Management

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: Citrix releases urgent patches for two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, in NetScaler ADC and Gateway under active exploitation.

item.title: UPDATE: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Actively Exploited in the Wild
item.description:
Headline: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Actively Exploited in the Wild

Summary:
Unit 42 has issued a threat brief concerning two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, affecting Citrix NetScaler devices. Both vulnerabilities have been assigned a CVSS v4.0 base score of 9.5 and are confirmed to be actively exploited in the wild. According to telemetry from Palo Alto Networks Cortex Xpanse, over 50,000 NetScaler instances are exposed and potentially vulnerable globally. Organizations are urged to apply the latest security updates from Citrix immediately. The advisory warns that patching alone will not remove existing compromises, and recommends that organizations hunt for signs of post-exploitation activity. While specific TTPs have not been released, general threat hunting guidance is provided.

Summary:

The intrusion originated from Adif's web infrastructure and served as a pivot point into Renfe's network, resulting in the exfiltration of 500 GB of data, including employee records. Headline: Phishing Campaigns Bypass MFA with Device Code Flow to Hit M365 Users

Summary:
Threat actors are deploying sophisticated phishing kits like 'N0va' and 'CSuite' in campaigns targeting Microsoft 365 users across the U.S. and Europe. These attacks use a technique known as Device Code phishing, which tricks users into authorizing a malicious application through a legitimate Microsoft authentication flow. This method allows attackers to steal access and refresh tokens, granting them persistent access to the victim's account and effectively bypassing multi-factor authentication (MFA).

item.title: UPDATE: FBI Warns of OAuth Consent Phishing Campaign Bypassing MFA
item.description:
Headline: FBI Warns of OAuth Consent Phishing Campaign Bypassing MFA

Summary:
The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) has issued a public service announcement about a sophisticated 'OAuth consent phishing' campaign targeting high-profile individuals since late 2025. Attackers use social engineering to trick victims into granting a malicious application permissions to their cloud accounts (e.g., Google, Microsoft). This provides the attacker with persistent access that bypasses both passwords and multi-factor authentication (MFA), as access is token-based. Changing the account password does not revoke this access.

Severity: High

Categories: Phishing, Threat Intelligence, Cloud Security

Article Type: Advisory

Reading Time: 5 minutes

Meta Description: The FBI warns of an ongoing 'OAuth consent phishing' campaign where attackers trick users into granting malicious apps persistent, token-based account access.
